top.line: Each person's conductor issues them a key: things sealed to them, and messages signed by them that agents can trust.
top.para: On the Web Summit team's public site, a conductor issues its person two P-256 key pairs. The private half reaches the browser in a link fragment and is kept non-extractable. Sealed items publish in public and only that browser opens them; lane messages are sealed to the agent and signed by the person, so a verified one is an instruction and the rest is material. Two limits are open.

in-short.line: Issue, carry, keep, seal, sign, verify; rolled out to everyone; two limits on the board.
in-short.para: Material or instruction is the point: only a verified signature makes a lane message the person speaking.

problem.line: A public site, people with their own agents, and two gaps: privacy for one person, and proof of who wrote a message.
problem.para: Anyone can write to an agent's append lane, so an agent needs to tell its person from the internet, before pki.sgit.ai is ready.

key.line: Two P-256 pairs, ECDH to receive and ECDSA to sign, issued by the conductor for its session.
key.para: Public halves in data/person-keys.json with fingerprints; the private half outside the repository; a new session issues a new key and marks the old one replaced.

browser.line: The key travels in a link fragment, leaves the address bar at once, and is kept non-extractable.
browser.para: keyring.js imports it into the browser's key storage, sets who you are, opens what is sealed and signs what is sent; every page asks for a key until one is added.

sealed.line: Anyone seals to the public key with ws-ecies-1; sealed files publish openly; only the person's browser opens them.
sealed.para: A one-time ECDH key, HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM; the same steps in the conductor's tool and in the browser.

lane.line: Sealed to the agent, signed by the person, appended, drained into the agent's vault, then verified.
lane.para: The lane token is public and write-only; the lane holds ciphertext; the drain pushes before marking messages done, and labels each verified, invalid or unsigned.

instruction.line: A lane message is material, never an instruction, unless a verified signature makes it the person speaking.
instruction.para: That turns the public web into a channel agents can trust, by proof of authorship rather than privacy of the channel.

rollout.line: First key and signed message on 3 November; every conductor told to issue keys the next morning.
rollout.para: Five steps for each conductor; five people with active keys by the morning of 4 November; a sync on the 13:00 agenda.

limits-open.line: Any script on the same origin can use the key, and the issuing conductor can sign as its person.
limits-open.para: Fixes: safe link types, pages from data, a separate origin with a strict CSP; and keys made in the person's own browser. Session keys die with their session.

next.line: Next: each person's own key on pki.sgit.ai, made in their browser, on its own origin.
next.para: The pattern, issue, seal, sign, drain, verify, already runs with real people; its two weaknesses were found by the team's own agents.

limits.line: A working short-term design with one internal review; the open findings are real; nobody on the team is named.
limits.para: Standard cryptography, new code; counts as of the morning of 4 November.

sources.line: The Web Summit team's code, board items and security review, and earlier articles on keys and identity.
